- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.20) and price is rising, model frequently fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast by 2–4% in next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates prices during mean-reversion phases (e.g., after 3+ consecutive days of decline); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply a 1–3% smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecasted path.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% in the 2nd–3rd day of recovery.
